findings.text: Early breakpoint init discovers breakpoint and watchpoint register counts, announces them, registers a hotplug starting callback for breakpoint reset, installs the same reset routine as the suspend restore hook, and returns the hotplug registration status.
Suspend debug restorer is single assignment: if a hook is already installed the request warns and keeps the existing hook, otherwise it stores the supplied callback for later resume use.
Perf read hook for hardware breakpoints performs no action, and the breakpoint exception notifier unconditionally reports that it took no action.

Hyp stub vector table provides sixteen ordered slots for four execution states with sync plus IRQ plus FIQ plus error entries each; the EL2h and 64-bit EL1 sync slots share a common dispatcher while the remaining slots use invalid handlers.

Sync dispatcher selects by hypercall identity: set vectors updates EL2 vector base and succeeds, finalize transfers to EL2 finalization, virtual GIC feature query returns that register, soft restart shuffles argument registers and branches without returning, reset vectors succeeds as a no-op, and any other identity fails with a stub error.

EL2 finalization rejects when the EL2 MMU is enabled, when VHE is unsupported, or when an override requests hypervisor-only VHE; otherwise it installs host VHE controls, adopts the EL1 stack, carries floating point plus vector base plus memory controls from EL1 to EL2 with conditional TCR2 and permission indirection state, restricts profiling controls from EL1, rewrites saved status to remain at EL2, and continues into VHE entry.

VHE entry invalidates EL1 TLB state with barriers, enables the EL2 stage one MMU using transferred EL1 configuration, disables the EL1 stage one MMU, clears the return value and returns from the exception.

Two helpers issue stub hypercalls: one always requests vector reset, the other requests EL2 finalization only when boot mode was EL2 and current level is EL1, otherwise returning without issuing the call.
Idle behavior is chosen among wait for interrupt, yield hint, and no-operation, defaulting to wait for interrupt; an early boot parameter selects one named mode and rejects missing or unknown values.

Idle entry saves interrupt context, then either waits for interrupt with a barrier, executes a yield hint with a barrier, or does nothing further for no-operation mode, before restoring interrupt context; the architecture idle entry delegates to this routine.

Image header flags combine endianness plus page size plus physical base fields at defined shifts; page size derives from page shift, endianness selects a build dependent variant, physical base marker is set, and size and flag values are emitted as little endian low and high halves with byte swap handling.
Headers use include guards and define assertions away; startup symbol export creates an aliased provider symbol and link-time checks that the source lies before BSS so BSS symbols cannot be exported.
Per CPU state comprises an NMI context record, an IRQ stack pointer, and a shadow call stack pointer for IRQ use.

Early init allocates one IRQ stack per possible CPU with node affinity and, only when shadow call stacks are enabled, one shadow stack per possible CPU, failing with out of memory if any allocation fails.

Architecture IRQ and FIQ dispatch pointers start at default handlers and are writable only during early init; registration succeeds once and rejects a second distinct root handler as busy while logging the chosen handler.
IRQ subsystem init aborts if stack allocation fails, initializes the interrupt chip, and when priority masking is used checks async abort masking before restoring a no-IRQ process context mask.
Soft interrupt processing on its own stack runs through a small trampoline that invokes generic softirq handling on the IRQ stack.

Jump label patching writes either a branch to the jump target or a no-operation at the patched address without synchronizing, and a separate apply step synchronizes all CPUs after a batch of queued patches.

Address randomization defaults to disabled and becomes enabled only when not disabled on the command line and when observed image displacement reaches the minimum alignment, otherwise staying disabled; the no-randomization boot parameter handler is a no-op.
Kexec image probe accepts a buffer only when large enough for an image header and when its magic matches the expected ARM64 image magic.

Kexec image load rejects zero image size, endian mismatch without mixed endian support, and page size markers without matching granule support, then places the kernel buffer with minimum alignment while accounting for text offset, repeatedly advancing past unsuitable holes until companion segments fit, finally trimming text offset and setting entry to the adjusted base.

Companion segment loading reserves addresses above the kernel, optionally adds a top-down crash header with large page alignment plus encrypted volume keys for crash images, places an initrd inside a bounded window above an aligned base, then builds packs and places the device tree top-down with two megabyte alignment, restoring segment count and releasing the tree on failure.
Kexec file operations bind image probe and load routines, with signature verification present only under image signature verification builds; the loader uses its own log prefix.

Debugger register table maps general registers plus stack pointer plus program counter to trap frame offsets with eight byte width, maps program status as four bytes with a big endian adjustment, and lists vector plus floating point status registers as sixteen or four byte entries with no trap frame mapping.

Debugger register access bounds checks the register number, copies to or from the trap frame when mapped, returns zeroes on unmapped reads and success without write on unmapped writes, fails out of range access, and read also returns the register name.

Hard failures abort when IRQ stacks cannot be allocated or when IRQ or FIQ arrives without a registered root handler; recoverable failures report busy on duplicate handler registration, invalid argument on malformed debugger or kexec inputs, out of memory on stack allocation failure, and stub error on unsupported stub hypercalls or ineligible EL2 finalization.

No explicit locks appear; exclusion relies on early init single threading plus read-only-after-init dispatch pointers plus single-assignment guards for suspend restorer and handler registration plus per-CPU stacks and contexts that avoid sharing.
